subject: maths
title: Chapter 9 · Test 2
summary: Chapter 9 test 2: 15 questions on sampling, box plots, standard deviation, scatterplots, time series and evaluating statistical reports.
body: This test covers Chapter 9 · Statistics: collecting data and sampling, box plots and the five-number summary, standard deviation, scatterplots and lines of best fit, time-series data and evaluating statistical reports. It has 15 multiple-choice questions, from easy to challenge. Allow about 25 minutes and work with no notes. A calculator is allowed for this test, but show your working on paper so you can check each step. Many questions use a graph or diagram — read the axes and scales carefully before you answer.

questions.prompt: In which situation is a census (rather than a sample) the sensible choice?

options.A: Recording the age of every student in a class of 25 for the class roll
options.B: Testing how long light globes last before they burn out
options.C: Finding the average height of all Australian adults
options.D: Taste-testing a large pot of soup

questions.explanation: A class of 25 is small and the roll needs every student, so a census is sensible. Testing light globes destroys them, so a sample must be used.
steps: A census is sensible when the population is small or every member is needed.
A class roll needs all 25 students, and 25 is small — a census.

mistakes.B: Step 2: testing destroys the globes, so you can only test a sample.
mistakes.C: Step 1: measuring millions of people is far too costly — a sample is used.
mistakes.D: Step 2: tasting the whole pot would leave no soup — one spoonful (a sample) is enough.

questions.topic: Box plots and the five-number summary
questions.prompt: The box plot shows a basketball team's points per game. What is the range?
questions.explanation: Range = maximum − minimum = 47 − 15 = 32. The length of the box (12) is the IQR, not the range.
steps: Read the ends of the whiskers: minimum 15, maximum 47.

mistakes.A: Step 1: 34 − 22 = 12 is the IQR (the box). The range uses the whisker ends.
mistakes.B: Step 1: 47 is the maximum. Subtract the minimum.
mistakes.D: Step 1: 30 is the median. The range is maximum − minimum.

questions.diagram_alt: A box plot of points per game on a scale from 10 to 50: minimum 15, Q1 22, median 30, Q3 34, maximum 47

questions.prompt: Two archers each fired 9 arrows. Their scores are in the dot plots, and both have a mean of 8. Which archer is more consistent?

options.A: Archer Y, because the scores are more spread out
options.B: Archer X, because the scores are closer to the mean (smaller standard deviation)
options.C: Both, because the means are equal
options.D: Archer Y, because the highest score is 13

questions.explanation: Archer X's scores are all within 2 of the mean, so the standard deviation is smaller and X is more consistent. Archer Y's spread from 3 to 13 shows less consistency.
steps: Consistency means the values stay close to the mean — a small standard deviation.
Archer X's scores (6 to 10) are bunched around 8; Archer Y's (3 to 13) are spread out. So Archer X is more consistent.

mistakes.A: Step 2: more spread out means LESS consistent — a larger standard deviation.
mistakes.C: Step 1: equal means say nothing about consistency. Compare the spread.
mistakes.D: Step 1: one high score does not make an archer consistent. Look at the spread of all the scores.

questions.diagram_alt: Two dot plots on a scale from 2 to 14. Archer X: 6, 7, 7, 8, 8, 8, 9, 9, 10. Archer Y: 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13

questions.topic: Scatterplots and lines of best fit
questions.prompt: Which describes a good line of best fit drawn by eye?

options.A: A line joining every point from left to right
options.B: A line through the first and last points
options.C: A line that must pass through the origin (0, 0)
options.D: A straight line following the trend, with about the same number of points above and below it

questions.explanation: A line of best fit is one straight line through the middle of the pattern, with roughly equal numbers of points on each side. Joining the dots is not a line of best fit.
steps: A line of best fit shows the overall trend: one straight line through the middle of the dots.
It should have roughly the same number of points above and below it.

mistakes.A: Step 1: joining the dots is not a line of best fit. Draw ONE straight line through the middle.
mistakes.B: Step 2: the first and last points may not follow the trend. Balance the points above and below.
mistakes.C: Step 2: a line of best fit goes wherever the trend goes; it does not have to pass through (0, 0).

questions.topic: Box plots and the five-number summary
questions.prompt: Find the lower quartile (Q1) of these 10 values: 4, 7, 8, 10, 12, 15, 16, 19, 21, 25.
questions.explanation: The lower half is 4, 7, 8, 10, 12, whose median is 8. The median of all 10 values (13.5) is not Q1.
steps: 10 values: the lower half is the first 5 values: 4, 7, 8, 10, 12.
Q1 = the middle of these = 8.

mistakes.A: Step 2: the lower half is the first 5 values (4, 7, 8, 10, 12). Its middle value is the 3rd one — no averaging needed.
mistakes.C: Step 1: 13.5 is the median of the whole data set. Q1 is the median of the lower half.
mistakes.D: Step 2: 19 is the median of the UPPER half, which is Q3.

questions.prompt: The graph shows a town's annual rainfall from 2018 to 2024. What is the percentage decrease from 2018 to 2024?
questions.explanation: The fall is 800 − 680 = 120 mm, and 120 ÷ 800 × 100 = 15%. Dividing by 680 instead gives 17.6%.
steps: Read the values: 800 mm in 2018 and 680 mm in 2024.
Decrease = 800 − 680 = 120 mm.
Percentage decrease = 120 ÷ 800 × 100 = 15%.

mistakes.B: Step 1: 120 mm is the decrease itself. Divide it by the 2018 value, 800.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you divided by the 2024 value (680). Divide by the starting value, 800.
mistakes.D: Step 2: 680 ÷ 800 = 85% is the 2024 rainfall as a percentage of 2018. Subtract from 100%.

questions.diagram_alt: Time-series graph of annual rainfall: 2018 800, 2019 760, 2020 720, 2021 750, 2022 700, 2023 690, 2024 680 mm; the vertical axis starts at 600

questions.prompt: Members of a library are numbered 1 to 450. A systematic sample of 15 members starts at member 9. Which member is the THIRD one chosen?
questions.explanation: The interval is 450 ÷ 15 = 30, so the members are 9, 39, 69, … — the third is 69. Using 3 jumps gives 99, the fourth member.
steps: Sampling interval = 450 ÷ 15 = 30.
Chosen: 9, then 9 + 30 = 39, then 39 + 30 = 69.
The third member is 69.

mistakes.A: Step 2: the third member is 2 jumps after the first, not 3.
mistakes.B: Step 2: 39 is the SECOND member chosen. Add one more jump.
mistakes.D: Step 1: 9 × 3 does not use the sampling interval. Find 450 ÷ 15 first.

questions.topic: Scatterplots and lines of best fit
questions.prompt: Which labelled point on the scatterplot is most likely an outlier?
questions.explanation: Point C (5, 9.5) is far above the straight-line pattern the other points follow, so it is the outlier. D is at the end of the data but still fits the trend.
steps: Picture the straight-line pattern of the points: they rise about 1 unit for each 1 across.
Point C is well above that pattern, so it is the outlier.

mistakes.A: Step 2: A sits close to the line the other points follow.
mistakes.B: Step 2: B fits the rising pattern of the other points.
mistakes.D: Step 2: D is the furthest right, but it still follows the trend. An outlier is far from the PATTERN, not just at the end.

questions.diagram_alt: Scatterplot of 9 points rising in a straight-line pattern from (1, 2) to (9, 10); point A is at (2, 3.5), point B at (7, 8), point D at (9, 10), and point C at (5, 9.5) sits well above the pattern

questions.prompt: A radio station asks listeners to phone in and vote on whether the speed limit should be raised. 400 people call and 70% say yes. Why is this result unreliable?

options.A: 400 people is too few to say anything
options.B: Listeners chose whether to call, so people with strong views are over-represented
options.D: Phone polls always give a result of more than 50%

questions.explanation: It is a self-selected sample: only listeners who care enough choose to call, so the result may not represent all drivers. The size (400) is not the main problem.
steps: Ask how the people were chosen: they chose themselves by calling.
Self-selected samples over-represent people with strong views, so the result is biased.

mistakes.A: Step 2: 400 can be a reasonable sample size. The main problem is HOW the people were chosen.
mistakes.C: Step 2: the percentage may be correct. The problem is who is in the sample.
mistakes.D: Step 1: that is not true. The issue is that callers chose themselves.

questions.prompt: Find the population standard deviation of 2, 4, 9, 9, correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.explanation: Mean 6; squared deviations 16, 4, 9, 9 total 38; σ = √(38 ÷ 4) = √9.5 ≈ 3.08. Dividing by 3 instead gives the sample version, 3.56.
steps: Squared deviations: 16, 4, 9, 9 — total 38.

mistakes.B: Step 3: 38 ÷ 4 = 9.5 is the variance. Take the square root.
mistakes.C: Step 3: √(38 ÷ 3) divides by n − 1. Population σ divides by n = 4.
mistakes.D: Step 2: (4 + 2 + 3 + 3) ÷ 4 averages the plain distances. Square each deviation first.

questions.topic: Box plots and the five-number summary
questions.prompt: The box plot shows a café's daily sales of a cake, with one low value drawn as an outlier at 2. What is the lower fence that makes 2 an outlier?
questions.explanation: IQR = 26 − 18 = 8, so the lower fence is 18 − 1.5 × 8 = 6. The value 2 is below it. Subtracting only 1 × IQR (10) uses the wrong rule.
steps: Read the box: Q1 = 18, Q3 = 26, so IQR = 8.
Lower fence = Q1 − 12 = 18 − 12 = 6, and 2 is below it.

mistakes.A: Step 2: 18 − 8 = 10 subtracts 1 × IQR. The fence uses 1.5 × IQR.
mistakes.B: Step 2: 12 is 1.5 × IQR on its own. Subtract it from Q1.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 26 + 12 = 38 is the UPPER fence. The lower fence uses Q1.

questions.diagram_alt: A box plot of daily sales on a scale from 0 to 40: left whisker from 8 to Q1 18, median 22, Q3 26, right whisker to 34, and a separate outlier dot at 2

questions.topic: Scatterplots and lines of best fit
questions.prompt: A line of best fit passes through (4, 70) and (12, 30). Find its equation.
questions.explanation: m = (30 − 70) ÷ (12 − 4) = −5; 70 = −5 × 4 + c gives c = 90. Using 70 as the intercept forgets that x = 4 there.
steps: Substitute (4, 70): 70 = −20 + c, so c = 90.
Equation: y = −5x + 90.

mistakes.A: Step 1: the line goes DOWN from (4, 70) to (12, 30), so the gradient is negative.
mistakes.B: Step 2: 70 is the y-value when x = 4, not when x = 0. Substitute (4, 70) to find c.
mistakes.D: Step 1: you did run ÷ rise. Gradient = rise ÷ run = −40 ÷ 8.

questions.prompt: A gym's ad uses this graph to claim "Membership has tripled!" By what percentage did membership actually increase, correct to 1 decimal place?
questions.explanation: Membership rose by 1080 − 1040 = 40, and 40 ÷ 1040 × 100 ≈ 3.8%. The bars only look tripled because the axis starts at 1020.
steps: Read the real values: 1040 last year, 1080 this year.
Increase = 40 members.

mistakes.B: Step 1: "tripled" comes from the bar heights above 1020. Use the real values on the axis.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 40 is the number of new members. Divide it by last year's 1040.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you divided by this year's 1080. Divide by the starting value, 1040.

questions.diagram_alt: Column graph of gym members: last year 1040, this year 1080, on a vertical axis from 1020 to 1090 with a zig-zag break

questions.prompt: Daily maximum temperatures in a city have mean 20 °C and standard deviation 5 °C. They are converted to Fahrenheit using F = 1.8C + 32. What are the new mean and standard deviation?
questions.explanation: Mean: 1.8 × 20 + 32 = 68 °F. Standard deviation: only the multiplying matters, 1.8 × 5 = 9 °F. Adding 32 to the standard deviation (41) is the trap.
steps: Multiplying by 1.8 multiplies both the mean and the standard deviation by 1.8: 36 and 9.
Adding 32 shifts the mean to 68 but leaves the standard deviation at 9.

mistakes.A: Step 2: adding 32 does not change the spread. Only the × 1.8 affects the standard deviation.
mistakes.C: Step 1: after multiplying by 1.8, add 32 to the mean as well.
mistakes.D: Step 2: multiplying every value by 1.8 stretches the gaps, so the standard deviation is multiplied by 1.8 too.

questions.topic: Box plots and the five-number summary
questions.prompt: The box plot summarises the marks of 28 students, and all 28 marks are different. Using the method in this chapter (Q3 is the median of the upper 14 marks), exactly how many students scored more than Q3?
questions.explanation: The upper half has 14 marks; Q3 is halfway between its 7th and 8th marks, so 7 marks are above Q3. Answering 21 counts the students below Q3.
steps: 28 marks: the upper half is the top 14 marks.
Q3 is the median of those 14: halfway between the 7th and 8th of them.
So exactly 7 marks are above Q3.

mistakes.A: Step 3: 21 students scored LESS than Q3. Count the marks above it.
mistakes.B: Step 2: 14 is the whole upper half. Q3 splits that half in two.
mistakes.D: Step 2: Q3 is the mean of the 7th and 8th marks in the upper half, so only 7 marks are above it.

questions.diagram_alt: A box plot of 28 test marks on a scale from 30 to 90: minimum 31, Q1 45, median 56, Q3 64, maximum 88
